# What evidence should decision-makers require from AI developers and deployers?

An exploratory research agenda on **AI evaluations, the credibility of evidence, and the institutional decisions that evidence can support**—especially as AI systems become more capable and consequential.

*Research questions and proposed methods, not an operational assessment service.*

::: {.intro-grid}
::: {.intro-label}
### THE QUESTION
:::
::: {.intro-copy}
_What can policymakers, auditors, and other decision-makers reasonably infer from the evidence presented about an AI system?_ 

Evaluations, safety claims, incident reports, organizational processes, and deployment outcomes provide different kinds of information. They also leave different blind spots. **AI Governance Evidence Lab** explores how to distinguish credible findings from unsupported claims, identify what additional evidence would change a decision, and design proportionate oversight under uncertainty.
:::
:::

## Research questions {#questions}

::: {.section-subtitle}
Three related questions, deliberately framed as possible research directions rather than completed findings.
:::

::: {.workflow aria-label="Three research questions and a proposed research process"}
::: {.step}
<div class="step-top"><span class="step-number">01</span><span class="step-tag">EVIDENCE QUALITY</span></div>
<h3>What makes AI governance evidence credible?</h3>
<p>How should decision-makers assess the provenance, independence, limitations, and reproducibility of developer claims, evaluations, audits, and incident reports? Which claims are actually supported?</p>
<div class="step-prompt">Sources · Incentives · Validation · Uncertainty</div>
:::
<div class="connector" aria-hidden="true">↓</div>
::: {.step}
<div class="step-top"><span class="step-number">02</span><span class="step-tag">MEASUREMENT</span></div>
<h3>What do evaluations tell us about real-world outcomes?</h3>
<p>Under what assumptions do benchmark results, pre-deployment tests, monitoring data, and observed incidents generalize to real-world risks or benefits? Where could statistical or causal methods improve inference?</p>
<div class="step-prompt">External validity · Measurement · Causal identification</div>
:::
<div class="connector" aria-hidden="true">↓</div>
::: {.step .step-final}
<div class="step-top"><span class="step-number">03</span><span class="step-tag">GOVERNANCE</span></div>
<h3>When should evidence change a governance decision?</h3>
<p>What evidence thresholds and escalation procedures could inform deployment, monitoring, disclosure, independent evaluation, or regulatory intervention? How should institutions act when uncertainty remains substantial?</p>
<div class="step-prompt">Decision thresholds · Accountability · Trade-offs</div>
:::
:::

## A possible research approach {#workflow}

::: {.section-subtitle}
A scoped research project could combine a literature and policy review with a comparative analysis of public evaluation and governance cases. Any empirical extension would depend on available data and feasible identification assumptions.
:::

::: {.output-grid}
::: {.output-card}
<div class="output-index">METHOD 01</div>
<h3>Map evidence requirements</h3>
<p>Compare public evaluation, assurance, and governance approaches; identify which decisions they support and what information they require.</p>
:::
::: {.output-card}
<div class="output-index">METHOD 02</div>
<h3>Analyze selected cases</h3>
<p>Trace claims to underlying evidence in a small, transparent sample; code gaps, uncertainty, incentives, and limitations. Interviews are optional and subject to access.</p>
:::
::: {.output-card}
<div class="output-index">METHOD 03</div>
<h3>Test decision implications</h3>
<p>Develop a decision-focused comparison of evidence thresholds or review triggers; use quantitative analysis only where justified by the available evidence.</p>
:::
:::

::: {.integrity-note}
<div class="note-symbol" aria-hidden="true">↗</div>
<div>
<strong>Research integrity and limits</strong>

A model-generated summary is not independent verification. An audit is not necessarily evidence of real-world safety, and an observed association is not necessarily a causal effect. This concept calls for traceable sources, explicit assumptions, consideration of affected parties, and clear separation between empirical findings and normative judgments. No evidence collection, interviews, model evaluations, or empirical validation have been completed for this concept.
</div>
:::

## Towards an Integrated AI Impact Assessment Framework {#framework}

::: {.section-subtitle}
A longer-term framework could connect structured evidence review, quantitative inference, and institutional decision-making. **This is a conceptual map, not a built platform or a claim that one framework can answer every governance question.**
:::

::: {.platform-panel}
<div class="platform-head">
  <div class="platform-eyebrow">PROPOSED RESEARCH ARCHITECTURE</div>
  <h3>Evidence → inference → decisions</h3>
  <p>Transparent assumptions · Independent scrutiny · Policy relevance</p>
</div>
<div class="platform-branches" aria-label="Three complementary research pillars">
  <div class="platform-branch">
  <span class="branch-number">01 · STRUCTURED ASSESSMENT</span>
  <strong>Evidence and assurance</strong>
  <span>Compare documentation, evaluations, interviews, stakeholder perspectives, and assessment methods (e.g., HIIG's <a href="https://www.hiig.de/en/project/impact-ai/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Impact AI Method</a>, as one illustrative framework).</span>
  <em>Which claims are supported, and what is missing?</em>
  </div>
  <div class="platform-branch">
  <span class="branch-number">02 · QUANTITATIVE EVALUATION</span>
  <strong>Measurement and causal inference</strong>
  <span>Examine uncertainty, external validity, deployment data, and experimental or quasi-experimental designs where credible.</span>
  <em>What can the available data actually establish?</em>
  </div>
  <div class="platform-branch">
  <span class="branch-number">03 · INSTITUTIONAL GOVERNANCE</span>
  <strong>Decisions and accountability</strong>
  <span>Study evidence thresholds, oversight incentives, independent scrutiny, regulatory choices, and organizational responses.</span>
  <em>How should institutions respond to the findings?</em>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="platform-foot">The pillars are complementary; none automatically establishes safety, social benefit, or regulatory compliance.</div>
:::

## A feasible first research output {#output}

::: {.intro-grid}
::: {.intro-label}
### DELIVERABLE
:::
::: {.intro-copy}
**Working question:** _What evidence should decision-makers require before relying on AI evaluation and assurance claims?_

A focused **policy research paper or report** could compare a small number of publicly documented assurance approaches, develop a typology of evidence quality and limitations, and propose decision-relevant questions for regulators or other oversight bodies. A companion evidence matrix could make the analysis auditable. The scope and final research question would be refined through literature review and expert feedback; this is a proposal, not a predetermined fellowship project.
:::
:::
